line: You're the new one in 3B. Lucía Reyes, 2A, right under you. Your shower drips into my ceiling, so we were going to meet anyway. Have you eaten?
choice2: Nice to meet you, Sra. Reyes.

line: Of course not. Saturdays I sort the food pantry at the parish hall. You carry two boxes, you take home a bag. Rice, beans, sometimes the good apples.
choice3: I'll think about it. I should go.

line: Behind San José, on Grand. Old roof, good kitchen. My son Daniel used to come with me. Now he's at the college, learning heating and air. He says Saturdays are for sleeping.
choice2: Heating and air is a good trade.

line: He's right, but don't tell him. Saturday, eight o'clock, side door. Wear shoes you don't care about. And tell me when you fix that shower.
My niece Brenda's quinceañera. The DJ wants nine hundred dollars. Nine hundred! For a man with a laptop. My sister says it's normal now.
choice2: Find a cousin with a laptop.

line: Lunch break. The hospital laundry is one floor down, no windows. So I come here for twenty minutes and look at trees like a retired person.
choice1: Mind if I sit a minute?

line: Can I ask you something? Daniel's college sent a letter about his financial aid. Four pages. I read it three times. Will you look at it with me?
choice2: I'm not good with those either.

line: Page two says 'verification.' They want his father's tax return. Héctor files every year. But the copy is in a box somewhere since we moved.
choice1: The IRS can send a transcript.
choice3: Let's find the box another day.

line: You see? This is why I ask you. Daniel would say 'Mamá, I'll do it,' and then it's April. Okay. Tonight I find the box. You come for coffee Sunday.
choice2: Let me know if you get stuck.

line: Héctor drives the number 6 bus. Yesterday two men got on at Fifth and asked a passenger for papers. He had to keep driving. He didn't sleep.
choice1: That's a hard thing to watch.

line: Ana's school sent a letter in Spanish and English. Side by side. Twenty years I've been reading those letters with a dictionary.
Every time I'm at the hall, you're there. Pilar has you on the coffee list now, I saw. Be careful. The coffee list is for life.
You don't come to the hall anymore. Too busy with the library people. It's fine. Just don't forget where the good coffee is.

choice1: I'm sorry I was short with you before.

line: Not now, I'm counting cans. Forty-one beans, nine tomato. Somebody gave us cranberry sauce in October.
